title: Bio-nano interfaces
alt: Artistic composition: two coated nanoparticles suspended above a flat lattice surface, with peptides adsorbed on the surface and small ion clusters between them.
note: Artistic composition, not a simulated system
description: An illustration, not a result. The elements are drawn from the systems we work on — a lipid-coated particle, a second particle with a different coat, peptides adsorbed on a flat nanosurface, free ions in solution — but they are arranged for the picture, at scales and distances that no single calculation produced. It opens the site because it is the one frame where the three lines appear together. Every other figure here comes from a real system.

title: Hairpins ordering on graphite
alt: Cyclic peptides folded into beta-hairpins, lying side by side in two ordered patches on a graphite surface.
description: Cyclic peptides that have folded into beta-hairpins and then packed side by side into ordered patches on graphite. Carbon is green, oxygen red, nitrogen blue, and the honeycomb underneath is the graphite basal plane. The point of the picture is the registry: the chains do not lie at arbitrary angles, they align with each other and with the lattice.

title: At the surface, up close
alt: Close-up of peptide chains lying flat on a lattice surface with pale ion clusters hovering just above them.
description: The same kind of interface from a few angstroms away, where the competition that decides everything is visible: the peptide backbone flat against the lattice, and the hydrated species just above it that the surface has to displace. Binding an ion in water means winning against that hydration shell.

title: A channel in its membrane
alt: Space-filling model of a two-subunit membrane protein embedded in a grey lipid bilayer, with a few lipids drawn in colour.
description: A membrane protein in its bilayer, drawn space-filling, with the two subunit colours showing how the assembly is put together and most of the lipid left grey. The lipids picked out in colour are the ones being followed. Nearly all of this work is done alongside an experimental group, and the simulation is there to explain a measurement.

title: A particle meeting a membrane
alt: Wide render of a dense nanoparticle core pressed into a lipid membrane seen edge-on, the membrane curving around it.
description: A polymer core pressed into a lipid membrane, seen edge-on. The membrane does not stay flat: it curves up around the particle and the lipids reorganise at the contact. Which membranes a particle does this to is set by the lipids it carries on its own surface, and that is the question the project asks.
